title: Q2 Product Update — Redwood Optimize & Dedicated Launch (Draft)
audience: All Redwood employees; primary read: engineering, sales, customer success, marketing
subject_lines: Upcoming: Q2 Product Update — Redwood Optimize & Dedicated
Heads-up: Product launch & all-hands talking points (Q2)
Draft announcement: Redwood Optimize + Dedicated capacity launch
content:
TL;DR:
We plan to announce two major Q2 items: (1) Redwood Optimize — a cost/perf toolkit that recommends batching/caching and quantization profiles for customers, and (2) Redwood Dedicated — GA for reserved GPU capacity with improved autoscaling and SLA updates. This doc is a working draft for the all-hands announcement, email + Slack copy, and an initial Q&A.

Key messages (single-sentence versions) - for execs:
- Redwood Optimize: smarter inference configuration that lowers per-token cost while preserving quality — now available as a self-serve product add-on and integrated into the Console.
- Redwood Dedicated: GA of reserved capacity with predictable throughput, burst options, and SLA-backed latency targets — aimed at mid-market and enterprise teams.

Longer form messaging (for email / blog / press):
- Why this matters: Customers tell us controlling inference economics and reliability is the #1 blocker to shipping LLM features. Optimize and Dedicated together give teams levers to reduce unit cost and guarantee performance.
- What’s new in Optimize: model-driven batching suggestions, cache policies, quantization profiles tested on canonical workloads; integrated evals to monitor quality regressions; per-route recommendations in Console.
- What’s new in Dedicated GA: configurable autoscaling policies, burst capacity, per-customer GPU pools, SLA options, private deployment compatibility.

All-hands talking points (CEO / Head of Product / Head of Eng):
- Quick opener: "Huge Q2 momentum — shipping features that customers have been asking for: cost controls + enterprise-grade capacity."
- Why now: converging demand for cost predictability + stricter enterprise SLAs. We can now offer both best-in-class serving runtime and tooling to quantify improvements.
- Impact examples: "We ran Optimize on a mid-market customer (ecom search) and reduced token cost ~28% with no measurable quality drop on their eval set." (internal case — cite later).
- Call to action: Encourage teams to review rollout plan; customer-facing teams to prep enablement; eng to monitor rollout metrics (latency, per-token cost, regressions).

Q&A (anticipated questions + drafts of answers) — keep answers short and conversational:
Q: Will Optimize change model outputs?
A: Optimize is focused on runtime and config changes (batching, cache, quantization profiles). We run evals per-model/prompt set and gate recommendations — customers can opt-in and preview before applying. If a quality regression is detected, recommendations are pulled.

Q: Who is eligible for Dedicated?
A: Dedicated is GA to customers on committed plans (monthly/annual). Sales will have a simple qualification checklist; SRE and Solutions Eng will handle sizing conversations.

Q: How does this affect hosted API pricing?
A: Hosted API remains available. Optimize is offered as an add-on for hosted and dedicated flows. Dedicated follows reserved capacity pricing models (commits + usage). Exact pricing details go to sales/package docs.

Q: Does Dedicated support private/VPC deployments?
A: Yes — Dedicated integrates with the Private control plane and can be deployed in VPC/on-prem options; some features require account provisioning and network setup (see linked Confluence).

Q: Is this backwards-incompatible for existing customers?
A: No. All changes are opt-in. We default to current configs; Optimize recommends but does not auto-apply without consent for production routes.

Notes to self / TODOs before publish:
- Finalize customer quote + permission (Priya) — high priority.
- Get benchmark screenshots and cost delta chart for slides (Samir).
- Legal to review public announcement language (Liam).
- Product Ops: finalize rollout schedule and enablement playbook.
- Marketing: draft email + blog post, coordinate timing with sales enablement.
- All-hands slide deck: 2 slides (What, Why, Impact + Next steps).

Distribution plan (draft):
- Internal all-hands next Wed (announce internal-first), followed by email to customers and blog post 24 hours later. Sales + CS to get enablement packet 48 hours before external announcement.

Slack/email drafts (short):
- Internal Slack: "Q2 product update: we're announcing Redwood Optimize and Dedicated GA at next week's all-hands. Draft announcement + talking points in my Drive — feedback welcome by EOD Tues."
- Customer-facing subject: "Introducing Redwood Optimize + Dedicated — lower inference costs + predictable capacity"

Open questions / decision points (brainstorm scratchpad):
- Pricing: do we want a per-route discount for early adopters? tentatively yes but need finance sign-off.
- Beta customers: who gets early access? propose top 5 existing enterprise users and 10 mid-market customers.
- Feature gating: should Optimize recommendations be auto-applied for new users? lean no.

Tone and style notes: keep internal comms celebratory but factual; focus on customer impact and next steps for internal teams. Avoid technical deep dives in the all-hands (save for follow-up tech sessions).

Intent: this is an internal-first draft — expect edits. I'm leaving fragments in places for quick edits (e.g., benchmark numbers). Once we have approved quote + benchmark images I'll convert to final announcement + slides.

-- Asha
short_summary: Draft internal announcement and all-hands talking points for Q2 launch of Redwood Optimize and Dedicated GA; includes talking points, Q&A, TODOs, and distribution plan.
